questions.question: **A **and **B **together can do a piece of work in 12 days. **A** alone can do it in 18 days. In how many days can **B **alone can do the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for finding the time of the second person when combined time and one person's time are given:

Days taken by B = (X × Y) ÷ (Y − X)

Where X = combined days of A and B = 12, and Y = days of A alone = 18.

Days taken by B = (18 × 12) ÷ (18 − 12) = (18 × 12) ÷ 6 = 3 × 12 = 36 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 12 days

Time taken by A alone = 18 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 12
 36
 3
 
 

 A
 18
 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units.

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = Total Work ÷ Days = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of A = Total Work ÷ Days = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of efficiency is x:y, the ratio of time taken is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done or in the ratio of efficiencies when the time period of work for all workers is the same.

Pipes and Cisterns

The same LCM logic applies where filling pipes have positive efficiency and leakage or outlet pipes have negative efficiency.</p

questions.question: A can do 50% of the job in 16 days, B can do 1/4th of the job in 24 days. In how many days can they do 3/4th of the job working together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Full time taken by A = 16 × 2 = 32 days.

Full time taken by B = 24 × 4 = 96 days.

LCM of (32, 96) = 96 units (Total Work).

Combined efficiency of (A + B) = (96 ÷ 32) + (96 ÷ 96) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

Time for 3/4th work = (3/4 × 96) ÷ 4 = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Work done by A in 16 days = 50% = 1/2

Work done by B in 24 days = 1/4

**Formula:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Time to complete full work for A = 16 ÷ (1/2) = 32 days.

Time to complete full work for B = 24 ÷ (1/4) = 96 days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Target Work = 3/4th of Total Work = 3/4 × 96 = 72 units

⇒ Time required = Target Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y:x.

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a work in X days and B in Y days, together they can do it in (X × Y) ÷ (X + Y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is the same as the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: Working together A and B can do a job in 40 days, B and C in 36 days and all three together in 24 days. In how many days can B alone do the job?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 40, 36, and 24) = 360 units.

Efficiency of (A+B) = 9, (B+C) = 10, and (A+B+C) = 15.

Efficiency of B = Eff(A+B) + Eff(B+C) − Eff(A+B+C) = 9 + 10 − 15 = 4 units/day.

Time taken by B alone = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 40 days

Time taken by (B + C) = 36 days

Time taken by (A + B + C) = 24 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of the time taken by individuals/groups; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

⇒ Total work = LCM(40, 36, 24) = 360 units

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 360 ÷ 40 = 9 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (B + C) = 360 ÷ 36 = 10 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 360 ÷ 24 = 15 units/day

⇒ To find B's efficiency: (EffA₊B + EffB₊C) − EffA₊B₊C

⇒ Efficiency of B = (9 + 10) − 15 = 19 − 15 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 days

**∴ The correct answer is 90 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Individual Efficiency Calculation

If efficiency of (A+B+C) and (A+B) is known, then C's efficiency = Eff(A+B+C) − Eff(A+B). Similarly, A's efficiency = Eff(A+B+C) − Eff(B+C).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals. If they work for the same duration, the wage ratio is equal to the efficiency ratio.

Combined Time Formula

If A can do a work in x days and B in y days, then together they can do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.</p

questions.question: 25 persons can complete a work in 60 days. They started the work. 10 persons left the work after x days. If the whole work was completed in 80 days, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 25 persons × 60 days = 1500 units.

If 15 persons (25 − 10) worked for the entire 80 days, they would complete: 15 × 80 = 1200 units.

The remaining 300 units (1500 − 1200) were completed by the 10 persons who left.

Number of days those 10 persons worked (x) = 300 ÷ 10 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial persons = 25, Initial time = 60 days, Persons left = 10, Total time taken = 80 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Persons × Days

 
 

 **Group**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Initial Group (25 persons)
 60
 1500
 25
 
 

 Remaining Group (15 persons)
 100
 15
 
 

⇒ Total work units = 25 × 60 = 1500 units.

⇒ Work done in first phase (x days) by 25 persons = 25 × x = 25x.

⇒ Work done in second phase (80 − x days) by 15 persons = 15 × (80 − x).

⇒ 25x + 15(80 − x) = 1500

⇒ 25x + 1200 − 15x = 1500

⇒ 10x = 1500 − 1200

⇒ 10x = 300

⇒ x = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

Total work is the product of the number of workers and the time they take. If efficiency is constant, W = M × D.

Chain Rule Formula

For different groups working on the same task: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂, where H represents hours per day.

Work and Efficiency

Efficiency of a person is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.</p

questions.question: A and B worked together and received a total of Rs. 18,000 for 15 days. A's efficiency in the work was 5 times that of B's. The daily wage of A (in Rs.) was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total daily wage of A and B = 18,000 ÷ 15 = ₹1,200.

Efficiency Ratio (A : B) = 5 : 1.

Wages are distributed in the ratio of efficiency: Total parts = 5 + 1 = 6.

Value of 6 parts = 1,200 → 1 part = 200.

Daily wage of A = 5 parts = 5 × 200 = ₹1,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount received = ₹18,000

Number of days worked = 15 days

Efficiency of A = 5 × Efficiency of B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ea5bf4cf50a9085505c3ce580480595a184d5310c52f8f2ef046197621dd3e6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Daily wage of (A + B) = Total Wage ÷ Number of days

⇒ Daily wage of (A + B) = 18,000 ÷ 15 = ₹1,200

⇒ Let B's daily efficiency be 1x, then A's daily efficiency = 5x

⇒ Total efficiency = 5x + 1x = 6x

⇒ Since daily wage is proportional to efficiency: 6x = 1,200

⇒ x = 1,200 ÷ 6 = 200

⇒ Daily wage of A = 5x = 5 × 200 = ₹1,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Wage Distribution Rule

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done, which is the product of Efficiency × Time. If time is the same for all workers, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Efficiency and Work Relation

Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency is the amount of work done in a single unit of time (per day, per hour, etc.).

Ratio and Proportion in Wages

If the ratio of efficiencies of two workers is a : b, their shares of the total wage will be [a/(a+b)] × Total Wage and [b/(a+b)] × Total Wage respectively.

questions.question: A and B can together complete a task in 18 hours. After 6 hours A leaves. B takes 36 hours to finish rest of the task. How many hours would A have taken to do the task, if he worked alone?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Remaining work time for (A + B) = 18 − 6 = 12 hours.

B takes 36 hours to finish this remaining 12-hour work of (A + B).

Efficiency Ratio (A + B) : B = Time ratio inverse = 36 : 12 = 3 : 1.

Efficiency of A = Efficiency (A + B) − Efficiency of B = 3 − 1 = 2 units.

Time taken by A alone = (Efficiency of A + B × Total Time) ÷ Efficiency of A = (3 × 18) ÷ 2 = 27 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) together = 18 hours

Work done by (A + B) in 6 hours = 6 ÷ 18 = 1/3

Remaining work = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ B takes 36 hours for 2/3 of the task.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 36 × (3/2) = 54 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 18
 54 units
 54 ÷ 18 = 3
 
 

 B
 54
 54 ÷ 54 = 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 3 − 1 = 2 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 54 ÷ 2 = 27 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Time and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x : y, then the ratio of their efficiency is y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If person A takes x hours and person B takes y hours to complete a work individually, then together they will take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual, which matches the efficiency ratio if they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: Three men and 4 women can do a piece of work in 7 days, whereas 2 men and 1 woman can do it in 14 days. Seven women will complete the same work in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equate total work: (3M + 4W) × 7 = (2M + 1W) × 14

⇒ 3M + 4W = 2(2M + 1W) ⇒ 3M + 4W = 4M + 2W ⇒ 1M = 2W

Total work in terms of women = (3 × 2W + 4W) × 7 = 70W

Number of days for 7 women = 70W ÷ 7W = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3M + 4W) complete work in 7 days; (2M + 1W) complete work in 14 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Efficiency × Time = Constant

 
 

 **Group**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 3M + 4W
 7
 14 units

 2M + 1W
 14
 1
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of 3M + 4W = 2 −−− (i)

⇒ Efficiency of 2M + 1W = 1 −−− (ii)

⇒ From (i) and (ii): 3M + 4W = 2(2M + 1W)

⇒ 3M + 4W = 4M + 2W ⇒ 1M = 2W

⇒ Substitute M = 2W in (ii): 2(2W) + 1W = 1 ⇒ 5W = 1 ⇒ W = 1/5 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of 7 women = 7 × W = 7 × (1/5) = 7/5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by 7 women = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 14 ÷ (7/5)

⇒ Time = 14 × (5/7) = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

M-D-H Relation

For group work, use (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂ to compare different sets of workers and work done.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the same amount of work. If Time ratio is x:y, Efficiency ratio is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals, which is (Efficiency × Time).</p

questions.question: A can do one - third of a work in 15 days, B can do 75% of the same work in 18 days and C can do the same work in 36 days. B and C work together for 8 days. In how many days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time for A = 15 × 3 = 45 days; Total time for B = 18 ÷ 0.75 = 24 days.

Total Work = LCM(45, 24, 36) = 360 units.

Efficiencies: A = 8, B = 15, C = 10.

Work done by B and C in 8 days = (15 + 10) × 8 = 200 units.

Remaining work = 360 − 200 = 160 units.

Time for A to complete remaining work = 160 ÷ 8 = 20 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A completes 1/3 work in 15 days.

B completes 75% work in 18 days.

C completes full work in 36 days.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Remaining Work = Total Work − Completed Work

⇒ Total days for A = 15 × 3 = 45 days.

⇒ Total days for B = 18 × (100 / 75) = 18 × (4 / 3) = 24 days.

⇒ LCM of 45, 24, and 36 is 360 (Total Work).

⇒ Combined efficiency of B and C = 15 + 10 = 25 units/day.

⇒ Work done by B and C in 8 days = 25 × 8 = 200 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 360 − 200 = 160 units.

⇒ Time taken by A to finish 160 units = 160 ÷ 8 = 20 days.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x : y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y : x.

Partial Work Rule

If a person completes 1/n part of a work in 'd' days, then the total time taken to complete the entire work is n × d days.

Percentage to Days Conversion

If p% of work is done in 't' days, total time = (t × 100) ÷ p. For 75% work in 18 days, Total Time = (18 × 100) ÷ 75 = 24 days.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a work together in 18 days. A is three times as efficient as B. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio (A : B) = 3 : 1

Combined Efficiency (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Combined Time = 4 × 18 = 72 units

Days taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 days

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by A and B together = 18 days. A is three times as efficient as B.

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Let the efficiency of B be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Then, efficiency of A = 3 × 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

⇒ Total work = Combined efficiency × Number of days taken together = 4 × 18 = 72 units.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total work ÷ B’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency-Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If Efficiency ratio is a : b, then Time ratio is b : a.

Combined Work Formula

If A does a work in ’x’ days and B does it in ’y’ days, then together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Man-Days Concept

The amount of work is proportional to the product of efficiency and duration, expressed as M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 6 days and 8 days, respectively. With the help of C, they completed the work in 3 days and earned Rs. 1,848. What was the share of C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of work/efficiency = Ratio of wages.

Total efficiency (A + B + C) = 1/3, A's efficiency = 1/6, B's efficiency = 1/8.

Efficiency of C = 1/3 − (1/6 + 1/8) = 1/3 − 7/24 = 1/24.

Ratio of A : B : C = 1/6 : 1/8 : 1/24 = 4 : 3 : 1.

C's share = 1/(4+3+1) × 1848 = 1/8 × 1848 = ₹231.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹231.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 6 days

Time taken by B = 8 days

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 3 days

Total wages earned = ₹1,848

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Wages ∝ Efficiency (when time worked is same for all)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A+B+C) − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 8 − (4 + 3) = 8 − 7 = 1

⇒ Ratio of efficiency (Wages) A : B : C = 4 : 3 : 1

⇒ Total ratio parts = 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 units

⇒ 8 units = ₹1,848

⇒ 1 unit (C's share) = 1848 ÷ 8

⇒ C's share = ₹231

**∴ The correct answer is ₹231.**

Work and Wages Principle

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person. If everyone works for the same number of days, the wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (Efficiency = 1/Time). If A takes x days and B takes y days, the ratio of their efficiencies is y : x.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time and Work, where an inlet pipe does positive work and an outlet pipe does negative work.
